topic: How should power margins for multihop routing adapt to varying node density over oceanic vs. continental airspaces?
consensus_response: Power margins for multihop routing should adapt to varying node density by dynamically adjusting transmission power based on interference levels, capacity, and latency. In high-density areas like urban continental airspaces, more stringent power control is required due to increased interference levels, compromising SIR. Conversely, in low-density oceanic airspaces, relaxed power control can increase capacity but compromise SIR. Adaptive Frequency Hopping (AFH) with Machine Learning can optimize frequency hopping patterns based on real-time node density changes, minimizing interference and maximizing capacity.
reference_context: The throughput requirement depends on the number of passengers using each service in aeronautical ad-hoc networks. The achievable throughput of aanets in oceanic airspace was better than that attained in continental airspace, namely 68.2 kb/s versus 38.3 kb/s, respectively.
